narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 73% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. That means, based on the academic profile reviewed, failure was judged more likely than success; it is a risk estimate, not a certainty about your ability.

The strongest factor was your third-year class rank: you were in the third decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. That comparatively low rank pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your LSAT score of 31 was the second-most influential factor; it is below the accepted-student average of about 37, so it also increased the estimated risk. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.70 was the third-most influential factor; compared with the accepted average of about 3.23, it added further weight toward a failure prediction. Other profile details, including family income and full-time status, were not among the top drivers.

To improve a future application, focus on the areas that drove this decision: raise your academic standing if possible, prepare for and retake the LSAT if feasible, and consider additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate record that demonstrates stronger academic readiness. Seek pre-law advising and a plan to show sustained improvement before reapplying.
